description: Kotlin type -> TypeScript type of the P2.4 type comparison (README "Types"). script-modules.json gives the Kotlin type of every parameter, return value and accessor of a @ScriptFunction / @ScriptGetter / @ScriptProperty (and of callable modules); kotlin_types.py maps each to a descriptor with this table, verify-surfaces.mjs (dts-types.mjs) compares it with the d.ts type. A nullable Kotlin type (`?`) adds null, and undefined for parameters (the OrNull converters take both). nominal is the type the d.ts is expected to say; accepted (parameters only, default nominal) is what the ScriptArgs converter takes; returns (default nominal) is the type of a returned value after ScriptArgs.toJs; open marks a nominal type that carries no detail (a d.ts type inside it is a refinement, not a narrower type).

kotlin.String.note: ScriptArgs.string converts numbers, booleans and script objects with toString; only null / undefined and symbols are rejected

kotlin.Double.note: ScriptArgs.double also takes numeric strings (roadmap appendix E of augment)

kotlin.Int.note: an integral value; the range is checked at run time, not by the type

kotlin.Any.note: a parameter takes any value but null and undefined (ScriptArgs.nonNullish); a return value is any value but null (Undefined.instance is a non-null Kotlin value); only the nullability is compared

kotlin.Unit.note: the generated binding returns undefined (ScriptArgs.undefined); d.ts void counts as undefined

kotlin.ByteArray.note: parameters take a Java byte[] or an array of numbers (ScriptArgs.bytes); a returned byte[] stays a Java array, which the d.ts writes number[] by convention (Q188 (a))

org.mozilla.javascript.NativeArray.note: arrays are compared regardless of readonly (a d.ts T[] or readonly T[] is a refinement)

org.mozilla.javascript.NativeObject.note: a plain script object; d.ts option and result interfaces are refinements

collections.note: Parameters (ScriptArgs.list / map) take a script array or Java list, a plain object or Java map: readonly unknown[] / object. Returned lists become script arrays of the mapped element type (RhinoUtils.toJsValue; unknown when the element is not mapped), compared as readonly arrays, returned maps with string keys plain objects (object).

unmapped.kotlin.Any?: no type: the parameter takes any script value, the function checks it itself (raw parameter) or returns any value
unmapped.org.autojs.autojs.rhino.ProxyObject: a dynamic script object whose members the implementation defines at run time
unmapped.org.autojs.autojs.rhino.ProxyJavaObject: a dynamic script object whose members the implementation defines at run time
unmapped.kotlin.collections.Set: returned as a Java Set: RhinoUtils.toJsValue converts only arrays, lists and string-keyed maps
unmapped.kotlin.collections.MutableSet: returned as a Java Set (see kotlin.collections.Set)

javaClasses: A Java or Kotlin class in returned-objects.json is compared with the d.ts type of the object's probe; any other class with the d.ts type of its qualified name (`org.opencv.core.Point`); a class the d.ts does not declare is unmapped (java-undeclared). Generic arguments of a class are dropped. Classes are open: a d.ts subtype (PReadableTextFile for PFileInterface) is a refinement.

levels.match: the d.ts type equals the implementation type (assignable both ways)
levels.refined: the d.ts type is a refinement inside the implementation type: literal types of a primitive, an interface for object / Function / {}, an array of a known element for an array, a tuple for an array, with the same nullability
levels.coerced: parameters only: the d.ts type is outside the nominal type but inside what the converter accepts (number for a String parameter)
levels.narrow: the d.ts type is a proper part of the implementation type: for a parameter it rejects values the implementation takes (often null for a nullable parameter; harmless), for a return value it omits values the implementation returns (null; unsafe)
levels.wide: the d.ts type reaches outside the implementation type: for a parameter it allows values the implementation rejects (null for a non-null parameter; unsafe), for a return value it declares values the implementation never returns (harmless)
levels.error: the d.ts type and the implementation type are disjoint
levels.unmapped: not compared: no Kotlin type (kotlin.Any?, @ScriptInstall names), a dynamic or undeclared class, or a d.ts any / unknown / unconstrained type parameter (reason dts-any)

reviewed.note: Known differences with a decision or an owner. Keys are fnmatch patterns of `<api> parameter <n>`, `<api> return` or `<api> value`, each for one level. check.py --strict-types does not fail on a strict-level position an entry covers (Q187 (a)); an entry no differing position matches is stale and fails. Entries on other levels only document the difference (types.json reviewed).

nodeReviewed.note: The Node runtime declarations against the same Kotlin types (Q186 (a), reported only): shapes that differ on purpose, keyed as reviewed above with the api of the matrix row. An entry no differing position matches is stale and fails; a difference without an entry is listed in summary types.node.unreviewed.

*launch*Settings return.reason: resolves nothing and rejects when the page does not start; Rhino returns whether it started

*startService return.reason: resolves the started component name or null; Rhino returns nothing

colors.toHs* return.reason: the float[] handle form resolves a Java handle (D-12); the plain forms return number[]

floaty.closeAll return.reason: resolves the number of windows closed (P3.3); Rhino returns nothing

images.compressToBytes return.reason: a Uint8Array, Rhino's Java byte[] as a Node binary (Q188 maps it to number[] for the Rhino declarations only)

images.loadAsync return.reason: Kotlin declares Rhino's promise object; Node resolves the image handle or null

*requestScreenCaptureAsync return.reason: Kotlin declares Rhino's promise object; Node resolves whether capture is available

images.recycle return.reason: resolves nothing and rejects on failure; Rhino returns whether the image was recycled

images.saveImage return.reason: resolves nothing and rejects on failure; Rhino returns whether the file was written

plugins.tools.callAsync return.reason: kotlin.Any is Rhino's promise object; Node resolves the JSON value of the tool

shell.checkAccess return.reason: a report per access kind (ShellAccessReport, P3.1a); Rhino returns a boolean

storages.removeSync return.reason: resolves nothing; Rhino returns whether the store existed

sysprops.get return.reason: the platform returns an empty string for a missing property, so null does not reach scripts in either runtime

timers.remove*Task return.reason: the member is the one of tasks, which resolves a boolean; Rhino's facade of this name returns null for an unknown id

util.*To* parameter 1.reason: the number conversion of Rhino's arguments takes numeric strings too (case util.dpToPx.string); the Node declaration states it

strictLevels.note: check.py --strict-types fails on these (the unsafe directions); without it the comparison is reported only (roadmap P2.4, decision Q187)
